summary: Round 8 (Missed-Offer Toast) validated end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_final_qa_r8.py — 9/9 pytest cases pass covering all 8 spec scenarios plus a cancelled-job sanity check. Frontend Playwright drive-through against the preview URL confirms the amber missed-offers toast renders on go-online with correct wording ('You missed 10 offers while offline.'), and the dismiss button removes it. Backend response shape is backward compatible: {ok, online, updated_at, missed_offers_count}. No regressions detected on /driver/live/offers or /driver/live/offline.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1624 — cutoff uses `since = max(since, cutoff_iso)`. Because ISO-8601 timestamps compare lexicographically, this only works while both strings are UTC with the same offset shape ('+00:00'). now_iso() and datetime.isoformat() with tzinfo=UTC both produce '+00:00' today, so it's safe — but a comment or explicit datetime compare would be more defensive.

server.py:1633 — cancelled_at exclusion uses {'$exists': False}. If any cancelled job stores cancelled_at=null (rather than omitted), it will be COUNTED. Consider `{'$in': [None, missing]}` or explicit `{'$eq': None}` semantics.
server.py:1630-1637 — candidate query has no index hint on (service_timing, dispatch_ready_at). At scale confirm a compound index exists to keep the 50-item limited scan fast.

Live.jsx:105 — setTimeout auto-dismiss uses functional updater comparing `v === missed`. Correct, but if a NEW missed count arrives before the 8 s elapses (edge case: rapid offline/online cycles), the older timer still fires; not a bug today but worth a cleanup ref in future rounds.
